findings.title: Reused namespace admission does not fail closed when Docker inventory commands fail
findings.rationale: The proposal requires strict refusal of pre-existing validation resources and preservation of those resources, but the supplied wrapper consumes docker ps, volume ls and network ls through process substitutions. Their exit statuses are not propagated by the enclosing while loops, including under set -euo pipefail. A failed listing can therefore be interpreted as an empty inventory. If Docker subsequently becomes available, execution can reuse an existing namespace and the armed whole-project down --volumes cleanup can remove its resources. The proposed observable-cleanup correction does not repair this admission failure. This concerns the wrapper explicitly being extended for Linux transport, rather than reopening a resolved provider or browser finding.
findings.suggested_action: Amend the bounded runner plan to require checked success of every Docker inventory command before resource creation or destructive cleanup becomes eligible. Preserve successful collision refusal and observable cleanup. Add controlled listing-failure cases proving that each failed inventory stops the invocation without running validation or issuing down against pre-existing resources. Keep these controls within the admitted wrapper/guard surfaces or ephemeral proof inputs.

findings.title: The declared coherence gate omits the new material assumption A-06
findings.rationale: The refreshed Assumptions Preview contains A-01 through A-06, with A-06 supplying the query/index premise for this renewal. Gate: Assumption Code Coherence still declares scope A01..05 and references a five-assumption result. The embedded approval and critique methods require coverage of the still-live assumptions before renewed approval. The supplied RED and source support A-06 as a planning premise, but they do not make its omission from the declared gate scope coherent. This does not require post-index performance results before implementation approval.
findings.suggested_action: Update the declared gate scope and supporting assumption evidence to include A-06, then obtain the fresh post-critique coherence result before requesting renewed approval. Bind A-06 to the frozen resolver, current schema and recorded PostgreSQL RED evidence; retain post-index plan and write-cost validation as subsequent delivery obligations.

overall_assessment: The managed composite index and shared all/RUNNER_SCRIPT design are faithful to the bounded intent. ARCH13-01 is substantively integrated through the common pre-product guard, independent retained invocation and explicit enforcement boundary. ARCH13-02 is substantively integrated through truthful full-build write locking, transaction-scoped statement/lock limits, disposable failure proof and conservative recovery. Two bounded planning corrections remain before renewed approval: fail-closed Docker resource inventory and complete declared assumption-gate coverage. No fresh evidence warrants reopening R01..05 or expanding into future providers, durable intent or unrelated architecture. PERF-01 and CIADM-01 remain delivery blockers pending approved remediation and evidence; this critique grants no execution or delivery authority.
recommended_path: Retain the proposed index and single lifecycle owner. Integrate the two findings, refresh the affected planning baseline and reviews as required, converge the coherence/scope/authority guards, and then request explicit v1.3 approval. After approval, require disposable migration and rollback proof, meaningful guard controls, executable isolated Linux rehearsal, invalidation and final authoritative all, refreshed PCV and complete independent audits before local activation and assisted IN/OUT. Keep remote execution separately owned and not_run until authorized publication and actual execution.
